```{r setup}
#| include: false
source("../../R/portal_config.R")
cfg <- portal_cfg
rel <- portal_release
v2_current <- rel$is_current(cfg)
```

Every column, event type and `info` field of the OPDI files
(default settings of the OPDI software), with the version columns and joins.
For what is published, see the [overview](index.qmd). The column tables come
from the software's own list of published columns, so they always match the files.

## How to read the tables

- **Type**: `string` (text), `double` (decimal), `boolean` (true or false),
  `date` or `timestamp` (date and time).
- **Unit**: every time is in UTC (Coordinated Universal Time). Altitudes are
  in feet (ft), distances in nautical miles (NM, 1 NM = 1,852 m), durations in
  seconds (s) or minutes (min), angles in degrees.
- An empty value (NULL) means the item was not detected or is not known. It
  never stands for zero.

## Flight list {#flight-list}

One row per flight. The file of a day holds the flights first seen on that
day (UTC). A **flight** here is a **track**: the position reports of one aircraft
that belong together. A track that holds several flights has one row for
each (see
[Tracks and flight identity](../algorithms/tracks.qmd#flights-of-a-track)).

{{< include _generated/flight_list_columns.md >}}

### How the airports were found {#airport-source}

`adep_source` and `ades_source` say how the departure and destination airport
were found, with one of four values; [Departure and destination
airports](../algorithms/airports.qmd) explains each case.

- `aerodrome`: An airport was named from the trajectory: from the first position (departure) or the descent near an airport (destination).
- `out_of_area`: Departure only: the track began in the air near the edge of the area covered, so the flight came from outside it. Not used when the area covered is the whole world.
- `undetermined`: No airport could be named.
- `runway_event`: The airport was taken from a take-off or landing detected on a runway, replacing the value found from the trajectory.

## Flight events {#flight-events}

An **event** is a moment in a flight, with a time and a position. One row per
event, in three parts:

1. the columns of the event, in the table below;
2. the [measurement columns](#measurements);
3. the columns of the event's flight, as in the [flight list](#flight-list)
   (`flight_id` appears once, among the event columns; the flight's `version`
   is `flight_version`, see [Versions](#versions)).

{{< include _generated/flight_events_columns.md >}}

Every published event has a time. Events the aircraft's own track clearly
contradicts, such as an in-block time while it is still flying, are not
published.

## Measurements {#measurements}

A **measurement** is a number attached to an event, stored as a column of the
flight events file and empty where it does not apply (see [Empty measurement
columns](#empty-measurements)).

{{< include _generated/measurement_columns.md >}}

Computed as in [Distance flown](../algorithms/distance-flown.qmd),
[Time passed](../algorithms/time-passed.qmd), [Holding patterns](../algorithms/holding.qmd) and [Point merge](../algorithms/point-merge.qmd).

## Flight index and catalogue {#flight-index-and-catalogue}

### Flight index

One file per month, `index/flight_index_YYYYMM.parquet`, with one row per
flight of the month. It tells which daily file holds a flight.

{{< include _generated/flight_index_columns.md >}}

### Catalogue

One file, `catalogue.parquet`, with one row per published day.

{{< include _generated/catalogue_columns.md >}}

## Event types {#event-types}

`type` names what an event is. A name with a part in braces stands for a
family: `xing-fl{level}` covers `xing-fl50`, `xing-fl70`,
`xing-fl100` and `xing-fl245`. Each row links to the page on how
the event is found and how accurate it is.

### Take-off and landing

- `take-off-roll`: The aircraft starts its take-off run. [Line-up and take-off roll](../algorithms/line-up-take-off-roll.qmd)
- `ATOT`: Actual take-off time: the wheels leave the runway. [Take-off and landing times](../algorithms/take-off-landing.qmd)
- `xing-runway-threshold`: The aircraft passes the runway threshold (the start of the landing part of the runway), a few seconds before touchdown. [Runway threshold crossing](../algorithms/xing-runway-threshold.qmd)
- `ALDT`: Actual landing time: the wheels touch the runway. [Take-off and landing times](../algorithms/take-off-landing.qmd)

### Other runway events

- `line-up`: A departing aircraft enters the runway to take off. [Line-up and take-off roll](../algorithms/line-up-take-off-roll.qmd)
- `runway-vacated`: An arriving aircraft leaves the runway after landing. [Runway vacated](../algorithms/runway-vacated.qmd)
- `runway-crossing-entry`: A taxiing aircraft enters a runway to cross it. [Runway crossings](../algorithms/runway-crossings.qmd)
- `runway-crossing-vacated`: The same aircraft leaves the runway on the other side. [Runway crossings](../algorithms/runway-crossings.qmd)
- `go-around`: An approaching aircraft gives up the landing and climbs away; placed at the lowest point of the approach. [Go-around](../algorithms/go-around.qmd)

### Block times

- `AOBT`: Actual off-block time: the aircraft starts to move away from its parking position (stand). [Off-block and in-block times](../algorithms/block-times.qmd)
- `AIBT`: Actual in-block time: the aircraft stops at its stand after landing. [Off-block and in-block times](../algorithms/block-times.qmd)

### Airport surface

- `entry-{element}`: The aircraft enters an area of the airport. `{element}` is `taxiway`, `apron`, `parking_position` (a stand), `threshold`, `hangar` or `deicing_pad`, for example `entry-taxiway`. [Airport surface events](../algorithms/surface-events.qmd)
- `exit-{element}`: The aircraft leaves that area, for example `exit-parking_position`. [Airport surface events](../algorithms/surface-events.qmd)

### Vertical profile

- `top-of-climb`: End of the climb to cruise, with the method of EUROCONTROL's vertical flight efficiency indicators. [Top of climb and top of descent](../algorithms/tops.qmd)
- `top-of-descent`: Start of the final descent, same method. [Top of climb and top of descent](../algorithms/tops.qmd)
- `level-start`: Start of a period of level flight, cruise included. [Level segments](../algorithms/level-segments.qmd)
- `level-end`: End of that period. [Level segments](../algorithms/level-segments.qmd)
- `level-off-climb-start`: Start of a level-off during the climb: level flight below the cruise. [Level-offs](../algorithms/level-offs.qmd)
- `level-off-climb-end`: End of that level-off. [Level-offs](../algorithms/level-offs.qmd)
- `level-off-descent-start`: Start of a level-off during the descent. [Level-offs](../algorithms/level-offs.qmd)
- `level-off-descent-end`: End of that level-off. [Level-offs](../algorithms/level-offs.qmd)
- `xing-fl{level}`: A crossing of flight level 50, 70, 100 or 245, up or down. [Flight-level crossings](../algorithms/flight-level-crossings.qmd)

A **flight level** is an altitude in hundreds of feet on the standard air
pressure of 1013.25 hPa: level 100 is about 10,000 ft.

### Distance rings

- `xing-{radius}nm`: A crossing of a circle of 40, 50, 60, 100, 110 or 120 NM around the flight's departure or destination airport (`xing-40nm` to `xing-120nm`). [Distance circle crossings](../algorithms/distance-rings.qmd)

### Holding

- `holding-start`: First turning sample of a holding pattern: a loop flown while waiting for permission to continue. [Holding patterns](../algorithms/holding.qmd)
- `holding-end`: Last turning sample of the pattern. Carries the holding measurements. [Holding patterns](../algorithms/holding.qmd)

### Point merge

A **point merge system** is an arrival procedure in which aircraft fly along
an arc, called a leg, at a fixed distance from a merge point until they are
sent directly to it.

- `pms-leg-entry`: The aircraft starts flying along a leg. [Point merge](../algorithms/point-merge.qmd)
- `pms-leg-exit`: The aircraft leaves the leg towards the merge point. Carries the point merge measurements. [Point merge](../algorithms/point-merge.qmd)
- `pms-merge-point`: The aircraft passes closest to a merge point, within 3 NM of it. [Point merge](../algorithms/point-merge.qmd)

### Airspace

- `xing-fir`: The flight passes from one flight information region (FIR) or upper information region (UIR) to another. [FIR crossings](../algorithms/fir-crossings.qmd)

### Track limits

- `first_seen`: The first position report of the track. [First seen and last seen](../algorithms/first-last-seen.qmd)
- `last_seen`: The last position report of the track. [First seen and last seen](../algorithms/first-last-seen.qmd)

Event types of earlier releases that are not published, such
as `take-off`, `first-xing-fl{level}` and `entry-runway`, are listed with
their replacements on [Releases](releases.qmd#moving-from-v0.0.2).

## Fields of the info column {#info-fields}

`info` holds extra details of an event as JSON text, for example
`{"apt_icao": "EGLL", "runway": "27R", ...}`. The fields depend on the event
type; a field without a value is left out. An empty `info` (an empty text)
means the event type has no extra details.

### Take-off, landing and other runway events

`take-off-roll`, `ATOT`, `xing-runway-threshold`, `ALDT`, `line-up`, `runway-vacated`,
`runway-crossing-entry`, `runway-crossing-vacated`:

- `apt_icao`: ICAO code of the airport.
- `runway`: Runway direction used, for example `27R`.
- `rwy_ident`: The same, under the name used by earlier releases.
- `runway_bearing_deg`: True bearing of the runway centre line, in degrees clockwise from true north.
- `traversal_class`: Class of the runway pass: `departure`, `arrival` or `crossing`.
- `align_deg`: Angle between the aircraft's track and the runway, in degrees.
- `max_gs_kt`: Highest ground speed during the runway pass, in knots (kt).
- `osn_flight_id`: Call sign received during the runway pass.
- `milestone`: Label of the moment in the PRU flight diagram (see [milestones of a flight](../algorithms/index.qmd#milestones-of-a-flight)): `T06` line-up, `T07` take-off roll, `T08` take-off, `T16` threshold, `T17` touchdown, `T19` runway vacated. The PRU numbered them for this diagram only; they have no official status and differ from the A-CDM Implementation Manual's milestone numbers. Not set on runway crossings.
- `method`: On `ATOT` and `ALDT` only: `acdm` when the time was found on the runway, as above.
- `height_reference`: What the height above the ground was measured from: `track` (the aircraft's own altitude on the ground at that airport) or `elevation` (the airport's published elevation).
- `bracket_s`: On `ATOT` and `ALDT` only: seconds between the two position reports the 15 ft crossing was placed between.

An `ATOT` or `ALDT` that could not be found on the runway is found from the
climb or the descent instead (see [Take-off and landing times](../algorithms/take-off-landing.qmd#runway-window-method)).
Its `info` holds `apt_icao`, `runway` and `runway_bearing_deg` (as above) and:

- `method`: `legacy`.
- `role`: `departure` or `arrival`.
- `bearing_error_deg`: Angle between the aircraft's median track and the runway, in degrees.
- `n_samples`: Number of position reports the time was found from.
- `at_track_edge`: `true` when the report the time comes from is the first report of the track (take-off) or its last (landing).

### Go-around

- `apt_icao`: ICAO code of the destination airport.
- `osn_flight_id`: Call sign received.
- `low_height_ft`: Lowest height above the airport during the approach, in feet.
- `recovery_roc_ft_min`: Highest rate of climb after that point, in feet per minute.
- `excursion_seconds`: Duration of the excursion, in seconds.

### Block times

| Event type | Field | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `AOBT` | `stand_exit` | Time of the exit from the stand this off-block leaves (see [Off-block and in-block times](../algorithms/block-times.qmd)). Absent when the part of the track holds no such stand passage. |
| `AOBT` | `stand` | Name in OpenStreetMap of the stand of `stand_exit`, when it has one. |
| `AOBT` | `apt_icao` | ICAO code of the airport of that stand. |
| `AOBT` | `first_seen_on` | Where the aircraft was when first received on the ground: `stand`, `apron`, `taxiway` or `other`. First seen on a taxiway, the time is mostly minutes late. Absent when the track holds the landing before the departure. |
| `AOBT` | `take_off`, `take_off_method` | The take-off of the same part of the track, and the method that found it (`acdm` or `legacy`). |
| `AIBT` | `stand_entry` | Time of the entry into the stand this in-block reaches. Absent when the part of the track holds no such stand passage. |
| `AIBT` | `stand` | Name in OpenStreetMap of the stand of `stand_entry`, when it has one. |
| `AIBT` | `apt_icao` | ICAO code of the airport of that stand. |
| `AIBT` | `landing`, `landing_method` | The landing of the same part of the track, and the method that found it. |

### Airport surface

`entry-{element}` and `exit-{element}`:

- `osm_id`: Identifier of the area in OpenStreetMap, the open map of the world. Where the aircraft enters or leaves several areas of one kind at the same report, the event names the smallest identifier.
- `osm_aeroway`: Kind of area in OpenStreetMap, for example `taxiway`.
- `osm_ref`: Name or number of the area in OpenStreetMap, for example a stand number.
- `osm_airport`: ICAO code of the airport.
- `opdi_time_in_use_s`: Time spent in the area, in seconds.
- `osn_icao24`: ICAO 24-bit address of the aircraft.
- `osn_flight_id`: Call sign received.
- `at_track_start`: `true` on an entry at the first report with a position of the track: reception started there.
- `at_track_end`: `true` on an exit at the last report with a position of the track: reception stopped there.
- `ground_only`: `true` on the events of a track that never leaves the ground and whose aircraft type is unknown or a vehicle type, in practice an airport vehicle.
- `encloses_stand`: `true` on the passage of a stand area that contains a smaller stand passed at the same time.

### Top of climb and top of descent

- `d200_time`: Time of the top as first found, before moving.
- `d200_altitude_ft`: Altitude of the top as first found, in feet.
- `relocated`: `true` when the top was moved, `false` otherwise.
- `analysis_radius_nm`: Radius of the analysis around the airport, in NM (200).
- `method`: `pru`: the method of the EUROCONTROL Performance Review Unit.
- `observed`: `false` when the track shows no altitude at least 3,000 ft below the top before it (top of climb) or after it (top of descent): the top is at the edge of reception.

### Level-offs

`level-off-climb-start`, `level-off-climb-end`, `level-off-descent-start`,
`level-off-descent-end`:

- `kpi`: ICAO indicator the level-off counts for: `KPI17` (climb) or `KPI19` (descent).
- `duration_s`: Duration of the level-off, in seconds.
- `distance_nm`: Distance flown during the level-off, in NM.
- `level_ft`: Altitude of the level-off, in feet.

### Flight-level crossings

`xing-fl{level}`:

- `crossing_seq`: Number of the crossing of that level on the flight (first = 1).
- `direction`: `up` or `down`.
- `bracket_s`: Seconds between the two position reports the crossing was placed between.

### Distance rings

`xing-{radius}nm`:

- `apt_icao`: ICAO code of the airport the circle is drawn around.
- `direction`: `inbound` (towards the airport) or `outbound`.
- `crossing_seq`: Number of the crossing of this circle on the flight (first = 1).
- `bearing`: Direction of the crossing point from the airport, in degrees clockwise from true north.
- `flight_level`: Flight level of the aircraft at the crossing.
- `bracket_s`: As for flight-level crossings.
- `position_jump`: `true` when the two reports the crossing was placed between imply more than 1,000 kt: the position stepped, as near areas of GPS spoofing.

### Holding

`holding-start` and `holding-end` carry the same fields:

- `holding_seq`: Number of the holding pattern on the flight (first = 1).
- `pattern`: `racetrack` or `orbit`.
- `direction`: Direction of turn: `R` (right) or `L` (left).
- `circuits`: Number of loops: total turn divided by 360 degrees, to one decimal.
- `duration_s`: Time in the holding pattern, in seconds.
- `distance_nm`: Distance flown in it, in NM.
- `altitude_start_ft`: Altitude at the start, in feet.
- `altitude_end_ft`: Altitude at the end, in feet.
- `straight_pct`: Share of the time flown straight, in percent.
- `context`: `arrival` (the flight lands at its destination within 60 minutes and 150 NM of the end of the hold), `en-route` (it lands later or further away) or `other` (local flight, no landing, three or more holds, or holds over half the time in the air).

### Point merge

`pms-leg-entry` and `pms-leg-exit` carry the same fields:

- `apt_icao`: ICAO code of the airport the system serves.
- `pms_id`: Identifier of the point merge system.
- `merge_point`: Name of the merge point.
- `leg_seq`: Number of the leg flown on the flight (first = 1).
- `direction`: Direction of flight along the arc: `cw` (clockwise) or `ccw` (counter-clockwise).
- `leg_distance_nm`: Distance of the leg from the merge point, in NM.
- `leg_level_ft`: Altitude on the leg, in feet.
- `duration_s`: Time on the leg, in seconds.
- `distance_nm`: Distance flown along the leg, in NM.
- `direct_to_distance_nm`: Distance to the merge point on leaving the leg, in NM.
- `direct_aligned`: `true` when the aircraft then flew straight to the merge point.

`pms-merge-point` carries `apt_icao`, `pms_id` and `merge_point` (as above)
and:

- `closest_nm`: Closest distance to the merge point, in NM.
- `via_leg`: `true` when the aircraft flew a leg of the system just before.

### FIR crossings

`xing-fir`:

- `crossing_seq`: Number of the crossing on the flight (first = 1).
- `fir_from`: The region left, for example `EGTTFIR`.
- `fir_to`: The region entered.
- `fl`: Flight level at the crossing.
- `bracket_s`: Time between the last position report in the old region and the first in the new one, in seconds.
- `airac_cfmu`: The AIRAC cycle of the boundaries used (524). An AIRAC cycle is the 28-day period in which aeronautical data such as airspace boundaries take effect.
- `airac_validity_start`: First day of that cycle.
- `airac_validity_end`: Last day of that cycle.
- `vertical`: `true` when the two regions lie one above the other (a lower and an upper region), so the crossing is a climb or descent through their boundary level.

### Events without details

`level-start`, `level-end`, `first_seen` and `last_seen` have an empty `info`.

## Source {#source}

`source` names where the position reports of an event come from: always `OSN`, the OpenSky Network.

## Versions and release {#versions}

Three columns say which method and release produced a row.

| Column | Where | What it names | Values |
|---|---|---|---|
| `release` | every row of both files | The data release; the same on every row. | see [Releases](releases.qmd) |
| `version` | flight list | The method that built the flight list row. | `v6.1.0` |
| `flight_version` | flight events | The `version` of the event's flight in the flight list. | `v6.1.0` |
| `version` | flight events | The method that produced the event. Different event types can have different versions. A method that changes gets a new version, so older data stay reproducible. | see below |

Event versions:

- `events_v0.5.0`: runway events, block times, airport surface, vertical profile, distance rings, `first_seen`, `last_seen`
- `holding_v0.2.0`: `holding-start`, `holding-end`
- `pms_v0.2.0`: `pms-leg-entry`, `pms-leg-exit`, `pms-merge-point`
- `fir_v0.2.0`: `xing-fir`

The measurement columns have no version column of their own:

- `distance_flown_nm`: `distance_v0.0.4`
- `time_passed_s`: `time_v0.0.2`
- `holding_duration_s`, `holding_distance_nm`, `holding_circuits`: `holding_v0.2.0`
- `pms_leg_time_s`, `pms_leg_distance_nm`, `pms_direct_to_distance_nm`: `pms_v0.2.0`

## Identifiers and joins {#identifiers}

- `flight_id` (a flight): The identifier of its track: the first 16 characters of the SHA-256 hash of the aircraft address, an underscore, and the time of the track's first position in seconds since 1970-01-01 (Unix time), for example `3f9a0c1d2b4e5f60_1781412334`. The flights of a track that holds several end in `-L1`, `-L2` and so on.
- `event_id` (an event): 32 hexadecimal characters, computed from the flight, the event type, the time and the version of the event. The same event gets the same identifier when a day is processed again.
- `icao24` (an aircraft's transponder): Six hexadecimal characters, for example `4ca123`.
- `flt_id` (the call sign): As broadcast, for example `DLH123`.

Joins:

- **Flight events to flight list**: on `flight_id`. Usually not needed: see
  [Flight events](#flight-events).
- **Flight index to flight list**: on `flight_id`; `file` names the daily
  flight list file that holds the flight.
- **Flights to tracks**: remove the ending `-L<number>` from `flight_id`.
- **OpenSky Network data**: with `icao24`, the call sign and the time span from
  `first_seen` to `last_seen`, the position reports of a flight can be fetched
  from the OpenSky Network's historical database, for example with the tools
  on its [data tools page](https://opensky-network.org/data/data-tools).

A `flight_id` depends on the method that built the track, so identifiers of
different releases do not match; see [Releases](releases.qmd). Join on `icao24`, call sign and time instead.

## Empty measurement columns {#empty-measurements}

| Measurement columns | Set on | Empty on |
|---|---|---|
| `distance_flown_nm`, `time_passed_s` | nearly every event | `AOBT`, `AIBT`, the four level-off types, and `ATOT` and `ALDT` found from the climb or the descent (`method` = `legacy` in `info`) |
| `holding_duration_s`, `holding_distance_nm`, `holding_circuits` | `holding-end` | every other event type, `holding-start` included |
| `pms_leg_time_s`, `pms_leg_distance_nm`, `pms_direct_to_distance_nm` | `pms-leg-exit` | every other event type, `pms-leg-entry` included |

Why some events have no distance or time:
[Measurements](../limitations.qmd#lim-measurements).
